newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks weaker, Zagrebacka heavily traded.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks weaker, Zagrebacka heavily traded.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended weaker on Wednesday, with turnover doubling thanks to heavy trade in Zagrebacka Banka, and market participants expected stronger activity to bolster prices this week.
"Trade was not too strong today, save for Zagrebacka," said Petar Vlaic of IB Austria.
"Prices could rise by the end of the week but I doubt higher levels will sustained in the longer term."
The bank took the spotlight of the day, selling 5,230 ordinary shares of which most went in a single deal at 2,070 kuna. It later lost 10 kuna to close at 2,060.
Preferred E-series added 20 kuna to 1,340 on volume of 976.
Zagrebacka's longer-term prospects were said to depend to a large extent on its perfomance this year. On Tuesday it forecast a 12 percent increase in the net profit for 1997.
"If that is all, (its price) might fall," Vlaic said.
The other leading stock Pliva pharmaceuticals lost four kuna to 460 after a mixed trade at 458-464 kuna in which 2,064 shares changed hands.
Food group Podravka, the market favourite in the past week or so during which it recovered considerably, was poorly traded with only 493 shares sold. It closed one kuna lower at 289.
"Buyers seem to have lost their interest in Podravka after the recent price increase," said one trader with a foreign client base.
Vlaic said the stock would not likely gain much more for now and foresaw its resistance at 300 kuna.
Overall, eight of 17 active issues fell, five rose and four closed flat. Volume rose to 13,554 from 11,597 units, with turnover more than doubling to 14.7 million kuna.
Dalmatian hotelier Suncani Hvar rose six kuna to 55 on volume of 1,292 shares, leading gainers.
Also among hotel stocks, Laguna and Jadranturist held their ground at 1,450 and 250 kuna respectively, but Istraturist lost six kuna to 164.
All had moderate volumes of several hundred units.
